title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a compact connected Riemann surface of genus g >= 2, with a base point x. Let H = PGL(2,C) (the transcription's 'PGL(2,C)[?]' is consistent with the 6g-6 count and with the previous page's G-bundles with Lie algebra g of rank 3).

Object. M^G(X) is the moduli space of analytic flat projective (PGL_2) bundles (P, nabla) on X that have no automorphisms. On the previous page Grothendieck computed the de Rham cohomology H^i_DR(X, ad P). Under the 'no automorphisms' hypothesis, H^0 = H^2 = 0 by Killing duality, and Euler-Poincare gives dim H^1 = 6g-6.

First claim. M^G(X) is the analytic space associated with a scheme (of finite type?) over C, smooth of dimension 6g-6. In modern terms this is the open 'simple' locus of the de Rham moduli space M_dR(X, PGL_2).

Second claim. After choosing the base point x, M^G(X) is canonically isomorphic, as an analytic space, to the space of representations rho: pi = pi_1(X,x) -> H with trivial centralizer, modulo conjugation by H:
  M^G(X) ≅ Hom^!_gr(pi, H)/H,
where ! means the stabiliser of rho in H is trivial. This is the Riemann-Hilbert (monodromy) correspondence onto the open free locus of the Betti moduli (character variety).

Bracketed NB. Hom_gr(pi, H) is obviously an algebraic space (indeed an affine scheme) on which the evaluation maps rho -> rho(gamma) are algebraic and H acts algebraically. Grothendieck adds, with a marginal '?' and 'sans doute', that the isomorphism above is not algebraic. This is the de Rham / Betti dichotomy: two algebraic structures on one analytic space, related by a transcendental biholomorphism.

Last line. The 'geometric' interpretation of Hom^! classifies triples (P, nabla, phi), where phi frames the fibre P_x ≅ P^1 (the next page confirms phi: P^1(C) -> P_x). So Hom(pi, H) is the moduli space of framed flat bundles, and dividing by H forgets the framing.

Purpose. Together with the next page, this is a plan to study uniformization through moduli of projective connections, organised in three steps:
- the mapping class group Out(pi) acts on the Betti side;
- Teichmuller space embeds via the Fuchsian monodromy;
- the space of projective structures (an affine bundle over H^0(omega^2)) maps to M^G(X) by the holonomy map.

Checks.
- dim Hom(pi, H) at a smooth point is 3·2g - 3 = 6g-3, and subtracting dim H = 3 gives 6g-6, which matches.
- Trivial centralizer gives H^0 = 0 and hence H^2 = 0, so the locus is smooth and the H-action is free (a geometric quotient as an algebraic space).
errors: Minor: for PGL_2, irreducibility does not imply trivial centralizer, since some irreducible (e.g. dihedral or Klein-four type) representations have finite nontrivial stabilisers. Grothendieck's 'Cent(rho) = {e}' condition is therefore the right one, but it is stricter than 'irreducible'. Also, freeness of the action gives only an algebraic space quotient a priori, consistent with his own 'espace algébrique' remark.

The claim that M^G(X) is the analytic space of a finite-type scheme is stated with a question mark and no argument. It is true (Simpson's de Rham moduli, or Nitsure/Laumon), but it is not proved here.
On the next page (not this one): the claim that the invariant domain D is unique is false for Fuchsian representations into PGL_2(C), which preserve both the upper and lower half-planes.

ideas.what: Moduli of flat PGL_2-bundles without automorphisms on a compact Riemann surface is algebraic, smooth of dimension 6g-6
ideas.modern_name: de Rham moduli space M_dR(X, PGL_2), stable/simple locus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Simpson (Moduli of representations of the fundamental group I/II, 1994); Nitsure; Laumon

ideas.what: Riemann-Hilbert: analytic isomorphism of the flat-bundle moduli with Hom^!(pi_1, PGL_2)/PGL_2 (free locus of the character variety)
ideas.modern_name: Riemann-Hilbert correspondence / de Rham-Betti comparison; character variety
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical monodromy (Weil, Gunning, Narasimhan); Deligne 1970 for algebraic vs analytic RH; Simpson for the moduli version

ideas.what: Hom(pi, H) is an algebraic space with algebraic H-action and algebraic evaluation maps; it represents framed flat bundles (P, nabla, phi)
The analytic de Rham-Betti isomorphism is (presumably) not algebraic
ideas.modern_name: transcendence of the Riemann-Hilbert map between M_dR and M_B (nonabelian Hodge theory)

missed.claim: The page explicitly identifies two algebraic structures (de Rham and Betti) on the same analytic moduli space of flat PGL_2-bundles on a curve and conjectures that the Riemann-Hilbert isomorphism between them is not algebraic. This is the basic de Rham/Betti dichotomy later made central by Simpson. Grothendieck frames it within a uniformization and projective-connection programme, with Teichmuller space and the Out(pi)-action on the next page.
missed.quote: Mais l'iso précédent sans doute n'est pas algébrique!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it documents an early, explicit formulation (undated, probably pre-1980s) of the de Rham versus Betti non-algebraicity for nonabelian moduli, tied to uniformization. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and standard by today's standards (character varieties, the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence, the de Rham/Betti distinction), and Riemann-Hilbert for flat bundles was well known in the analytic setting. The mildly notable point is Grothendieck's explicit remark that the comparison isomorphism between the two algebraic moduli structures should be transcendental, an early statement of a theme usually credited to Simpson. The page itself has no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: The superscript on M (transcribed as 'M^φ') is more likely 'M^G' (or M^G_g), consistent with the previous and next pages.
'avec ses[?] intérieurs[?]' should read roughly 'H opérant par conjugaison avec ses automorphismes intérieurs'.
The final line '(P, c, φ), (P, x[?], ...' most likely reads '(P, ∇, φ)', i.e. projective bundle, connection, and framing φ of the fibre at x; the next page confirms φ: P^1(C) -> P_x.
The illegible line after 'lisse de dim 6g-6, mais' likely concerns the algebraic structure not being the obvious one, or the analytic isomorphism; the exact reading is uncertain.
'Je vois immédiatement de faire' is likely 'Je vois immédiatement comment faire' / 'il est immédiat de faire'.
